body:
Found 2026-08-09. Updated same day after a peer session (CWNG READER) flagged a third producer;
verified in code. Context: workspace `notes/KOBO-ANNOTATIONS-WRITEBACK-INVESTIGATION-2026-08-09.md`.

`ub.Annotation.content_id` is populated with mutually unintelligible formats depending on how the
annotation arrived. There are THREE producers, not two:

1. **Device PATCH path** synthesises `f"{uuid}!!{chapter_filename}"`
   (`cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:177-180`) — e.g. `b3d1b38b-…!!chapter6.html`.
2. **`.sqlite` upload path** stores the device's raw `ContentID` verbatim (`cps/annotations.py:216`,
   from `cps/services/kobo_import.py`) — e.g.
   `file:///mnt/onboard/Author/Title.epub#(6)OEBPS/cha01.xhtml`.
3. **Web reader `create_annotation`** (`cps/annotations.py:616-621`) — synthesises the same
   `uuid!!chapter` form *only when the client omits it*, and otherwise takes the client's value
   verbatim. NULL when neither a chapter nor a uuid is available. This is now the most frequent
   producer, since the SPA reader gained note authoring (PR #1508).

**Escalation found while verifying (3): the value is CLIENT-CONTROLLED AND UNVALIDATED.**
`content_id = payload.get("content_id")` with no allowlist, no shape check, no length bound; the
code comment states the intent plainly: *"A directly supplied content_id wins."* So a client may
write an arbitrary string into this column — including a well-formed `uuid!!chapter` naming a
DIFFERENT book's uuid. Scope is limited to the caller's own annotations (`user_id` is server-side,
so this is not cross-user), which is why this stays data-integrity rather than security. But it
violates the project's own bar: *"Input validation on anything user-controlled reaching the DB …
allowlist over free-form; reject, don't sanitize."*

Impact: any keying, grouping, dedupe or chapter-level query on `content_id` is silently wrong
across the populations. A user who both syncs a Kobo AND imports their `KoboReader.sqlite` — our
documented recovery path, which we recommended publicly on janeczku/calibre-web#2610 — gets two
disjoint sets for the same chapters. It will present as "my highlights are duplicated / don't
match" long after anyone remembers why.

NOT established: whether a current code path joins on `content_id` in a way that produces a
user-visible bug today (the annotations view orders by `chapter_progress`). May be latent. It is
still a correctness hazard for anything built on the column, and the multi-device design now in
flight (`notes/MULTI-DEVICE-ANNOTATIONS-DESIGN.md`) leans on chapter identity.

Fix direction (not applied; the investigation was research-only and gated against schema/sync-path
changes): normalise at ingest to one canonical shape; **validate/reject client-supplied values at
the API boundary rather than trusting them**; decide whether the raw device form needs preserving
for round-trip — `device_origin_id` (`cps/ub.py:958`) already exists for device-side identity, and
the multi-device design proposes `AnnotationDeviceState.native_annotation_id` for exactly this.
title: content_id holds two incompatible shapes depending on ingest path
